To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bulk tank milk and penside oral fluids are effective tools in the surveillance of infectious diseases in livestock.

bulk tank milk and bulk tank milk-derived assays can be used as a proxy for individual animal milk and that bulk tank milk is a valuable tool in the surveillance of infectious disease in cattle populations.
bulk tank milk and penside oral fluid are effective for the surveillance of infectious diseases in livestock populations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of aggregate samples in the surveillance of animal populations for infectious disease.

the application of bulk tank milk sampling for the surveillance of mastitis, Johne's disease, and bovine tuberculosis in dairy cattle, and oral fluid sampling for the surveillance for bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis in cattle.
developing and evaluating new methods for the detection, estimation and prediction of disease in populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aggregate samples have been shown to be useful in monitoring disease, but that the utility of such samples in the surveillance of disease is limited to a few specific diseases.
aggregate samples provide a valuable tool for livestock disease surveillance.
aggregate samples are useful for monitoring disease and for estimating disease prevalence in livestock populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bulk tank milk is the best available sample type for the surveillance of dairy herds for mastitis, Johne's disease, and bovine leukemia.
bulk tank milk and bulk tank somatic cell count (BTSCC) are excellent indicators of the health status of dairy herds.
bulk tank milk and penside oral fluid sampling can provide a means to monitor the health status of livestock populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of aggregate samples is feasible and can be implemented in livestock populations to improve the detection of disease, estimate prevalence and monitor trends in disease distribution in space and time.
aggregate samples can provide useful data on the occurrence and distribution of infectious disease in livestock populations.
aggregate sample types provide a means to collect longitudinal animal health data from large populations.
